correctness.rationale: For Haar X, the paired displacement variables reduce to (uZ mod 1,vZ mod 1) with coprime u,v. Conditioning on Y=y yields v equiprobable inverse branches, whose u-images are the exact v-point grid. A length-L arc contains floor(vL) points plus one residual point. Bayes gives the asserted two-level density. Direct integration yields TV theta(1-theta)/(vL); the signed primitive has u zero-mean periods and range theta(1-theta)/(uvL), yielding exact arc discrepancy and all stated equality cases. Endpoint convention is immaterial to the density. Exact rational independent pushforward check produced 914 confirmations but infinite quantifiers are proved analytically.

originality.rationale: The 2020 primary paper performs gcd/Fourier analysis of the same two-time circle displacements to bound correlations for symmetric self-return events; we read its §6.1 through the two-time correlation calculation, and credit those ingredients. The new all-arc conditional density is a different, strictly more informative object: it implies sharp global and connected-target discrepancies and precise nontrivial event-level independence lengths. None of the inspected source statements contains these identities. A prior Fourier series may permit further derivation; absence from checked statements is not a guarantee of worldwide publication novelty. The closest October 2026 full published RESULT.md was also read: its exact symmetric-arc Bernoulli covariance kernel is preexisting and is not part of the originality claim; its main theorem concerns an orbit-pair variance, not this complete conditional law.
residual_risks: A Fourier-series evaluation of arXiv:2003.01361 §6.1 (6.3)–(6.4) may yield equivalent identities with further manipulations, so the originality claim is limited to checked published statements.

value.rationale: Existing two-time self-return studies need correlation control. The exact conditional phase law simultaneously determines all later-target probabilities, all conditional independence resonances, and the optimizers and sharp constants in disconnected-versus-single-arc mixing, with an arbitrarily large factor u. This is a unified structural classification rather than an isolated numerical instance, and it identifies an actionable distinction between strong and connected-target decorrelation.
